# Cached REST routes (the tier-2 catalogue)

One entry per cached REST route family: what it absorbs, the exact trimmed
shape it rebuilds, its query-shape guard, and what invalidates it. Extracted
verbatim from CLAUDE.md, which now carries only the contract and an index --
the depth lives here so it can grow.

The contract these all obey (reveal gate, absorb-and-rebuild, no URL keys,
explicit invalidation) is in CLAUDE.md under "The cache contract (three
tiers)". `GET /api/brief` on the dashboard renders the same checklist next to
the traffic that is still uncached.

## The routes

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path...}` (incl. `?ref=`, part of the key) — absorbs 200 file (base64), 200 dir (trimmed entries), **and 404** (the "config file absent" answer is half the win). One global row per (owner, repo, path, ref). Invalidated per PUSHED REF (+ the empty-ref default-branch spelling) by `push`, repo-wide by `repository` — see the dispatcher bullet's per-ref matrix — plus a **24h TTL backstop**.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits/{sha}` (`respcache_gitcommits.go`) — positive rows are immutable: no invalidation, no TTL, LRU-bounded only. Rebuild: `{sha, author{...}, committer{...}, message, tree:{sha}, parents:[{sha},...]}`. **Push payloads feed this cache too** (`absorbPushCommits`): each pushed commit is upserted once, globally; parents come from the payload's linear chain (`webhook.PushPayload.ChainedCommits`), which declines forced pushes, new refs, possibly-truncated arrays (≥20), and non-linear orderings rather than derive wrong parents. A **404 is cached as an expiring MISS MARKER** (`git_commit_miss_cache`, rebuilt in the contents route's `{"message":...,"status":"404"}` shape, 24h TTL) — a round-2 stance change: round 1 deliberately didn't cache these ("a missing sha can be pushed later"), but the dominant traffic is pr-minder's `mergeWouldBeEmpty` re-reading GC'd test-merge shas forever, each read a fresh upstream 404. Two bounds make it safe: the expiry, and the **clear-on-upsert invariant** — every real commit absorb (fetch, push payload, commits-list, compare) funnels through `ghdata.upsertGitCommit`, which clears the sha's marker, so a materialized sha stops answering 404 immediately; consumers fail open on 404 regardless.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits` — the commits LIST (behind reveal; pr-minder's fork-point base detection pages this per branch, dozens per sweep — the passthrough flood that motivated the route). Absorb-don't-byte-cache: each listed commit is upserted into the SAME global `git_commits_cache` rows above; a `commits_list_cache` snapshot per exact modeled query shape — key `(owner, repo, ref_param, per_page, page)`, where `ref_param` is the raw `sha` query value (`''` = default branch) — stores only the response's ordered shas (the rows+marker split the pulls list uses). A hit needs an unexpired snapshot AND every listed sha still resolving in `git_commits_cache` (an LRU-pruned commit degrades to a miss, self-healing; the re-absorb restores the pair). Hit and miss rebuild the identical trimmed item `{sha, commit:{author{name,email,date}, committer{...}, message, tree:{sha}}, parents:[{sha},...]}` — a superset of the one field the consumers (pr-minder `listCommitShas` + the reconcile hook's port) actually read (the top-level `sha`; they paginate by short-page detection, no Link header); the top-level author/committer USER objects, `node_id`, `verification`, `comment_count`, and every URL field stay dropped. Query-shape guard: only `sha` (non-empty), `per_page` (1..100, default 30), `page` (1..10, default 1) are modeled — anything else (`path`, `since`, `until`, `author`, ...) or a non-default `Accept` passes through. Unlike the pulls list there is NO full-page truncation guard: the snapshot IS that exact page's answer, and pagination continues under the next page's own key. Only a 200 absorbs (an empty array — a page past the end — is a valid cacheable answer); 404 (unknown ref), 409 (empty repo), 5xx relay unstored. Snapshots are flushed per PUSHED REF (+ the empty-ref default-branch spelling) by `push`, repo-wide by `repository`, + a 24h TTL backstop. The single-commit sub-path `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}` (a different shape; pr-minder's `commitAgeSeconds`) deliberately stays passthrough — since the commit-CI routes below registered the `/commits/*` subtree, that forward now happens in the subtree dispatcher rather than the router's NotFound.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{basehead}` — the three-dot `base...head` comparison (behind reveal; pr-minder's `compareCommits` — the `auto_open_pr` open gate + `closeEmptyAutoPrs`, repeated fleet-wide every 5 minutes by the pr-minder-reconcile hook: the ~90%-of-request-log passthrough flood that motivated the route). HISTORY: an earlier /compare cache was REMOVED because its trim dropped `files`, breaking pr-minder's empty-PR gate — this rebuild keeps every consumer-read field: `{status, ahead_by, behind_by, total_commits, merge_base_commit:{sha}, commits:[<the commits-list trimmed item shape>], files:[{filename, status, additions, deletions, changes, previous_filename?}]}` with the **files array's presence/absence preserved exactly** (consumers read `changed_files = files.length`; ABSENT = unknown → fail open, EMPTY = 0-diff → the close-empty gate) and the unread per-file `patch` never stored. The route is greedy (`compare/*` — branch names carry slashes); the whole trimmed doc is stored per exact `(owner, repo, basehead)` in `compare_cache` — the row also splits `base_ref`/`head_ref` into their own columns (round 2), which is what enables the per-ref flush — and the compare's commits are also upserted into `git_commits_cache` (synergy; a hit never depends on those rows). Shape guard: NO query params are modeled (`per_page`/`page`/anything → passthrough), only the default JSON Accept (diff/patch media types → passthrough), a basehead with a colon (the cross-fork `owner:branch` form — its fork side can't be invalidated by this repo's pushes) or without `...` → passthrough. A 200 absorbs the comparison; a **404 absorbs as an unknown-ref VERDICT** (a status-404 row, `{"message":...,"status":"404"}` doc — the fleet's close-empty pass compares `base...head` for fork PRs whose head ref doesn't exist in the base repo, a 404 repeated every sweep by design); 5xx relays unstored. A comparison (or verdict) depends on both refs' tips/existence, so a `push` flushes every row naming the pushed ref on EITHER side (`base_ref`/`head_ref` match; ref creation/deletion arrives as a push, so a verdict clears the moment its missing ref is created), `repository` flushes repo-wide (covering renames), plus the 24h TTL backstop.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/status` + `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-runs` + the raw statuses LIST — served under BOTH its path spellings: the legacy alias **`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{ref}`** (what the consumers actually send — required-builds' `listStatuses`; a GET-only top-level `statuses/*` registration whose wildcard is the whole possibly-slashed ref, so the required-builds status PUBLISH `POST /statuses/{sha}` falls to MethodNotAllowed → the proxy, pinned by a regression test) and the modern `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/statuses` subtree form; both land in ONE handler and ONE row space. All kinds are whole-document snapshots in ONE table (`commit_ci_cache`, a `kind` column: `status`/`check_runs`/`statuses_list`), keyed by the VERBATIM `{ref}` (a branch name — slashes and all — a sha, or a tag; NEVER resolved, so each spelling is its own row) **+ `per_page`/`page`** (round 2: required-builds paginates check-runs and raw statuses at `per_page=100&page=N` until a short page, so pagination joined the key — `per_page` 1..100 default 30, `page` 1..10 default 1, parsed like the PR-files route; the check-runs filters `check_name`/`status`/`filter`/`app_id`, repeated params, and out-of-range paging still pass through). The status/check-runs pair is registered as a `/commits/*` subtree dispatcher whose trailing-literal suffix anchor (`.../status`, `.../check-runs`, `.../statuses`) is what lets a ref carry slashes — a single-segment `{ref}` route parameter could never match one; every OTHER tail (the single-commit read, `/check-suites`, `/pulls`, ...) is forwarded to the passthrough proxy unchanged. Trimmed rebuilds: status = `{state, sha, total_count, statuses:[{context, state, description, created_at, updated_at}]}` (nullable `description` preserved; `sha` is the RESOLVED tip the answer described — exactly why pushes must flush branch-form rows); check-runs = `{total_count, check_runs:[{id, head_sha, name, status, conclusion, started_at, completed_at, app:{id}, output:{title}, details_url, html_url}]}` (nullable conclusion/started_at/completed_at preserved — consumers branch on conclusion===null; `app` trimmed to its id, the own-check filter field; `output` ALWAYS emitted but trimmed to exactly `{title: string|null}` — never the unbounded summary/text); statuses-list = a BARE JSON ARRAY of `{context, state, description, target_url, created_at, updated_at}` preserving response order EXACTLY (required-builds dedups by context FIRST-WINS relying on newest-first) with description/target_url nullable but always keyed. The blanket "no link fields" rule became a **pinned-allowlist mechanism** (the 2026-07-11 consumer survey superseded 2026-07-05's): the no-URL test takes an exact-key allowlist per route, and the per-status `target_url` + per-run `details_url`/`html_url` are pinned consumer-read exceptions (required-builds renders all three on its breakdown page) — adding another exception requires a fresh survey. Still dropped: per-status ids/creator, per-run `url`/node_id/external_id/check_suite/pull_requests and output's summary/text. Absorb gate: only a 200 whose body carries its array (statuses / check_runs / the bare array) absorbs — 404 (unknown ref) / 5xx relay unstored; an empty statuses array is cacheable. These routes deliberately do NOT read or write the `commit_checks` truth table: its normalized per-context rows are lossy against these responses (no timestamps, descriptions, or run ids); unifying the two representations is possible future work. Invalidation is the load-bearing part: `status`/`check_run`/`check_suite` events flush the payload-named refs' rows — the head branch(es) + the sha itself, every kind, every page (repo-wide when the payload names none) — `push` flushes the pushed ref's rows, and `repository` flushes repo-wide — so snapshots only survive while a ref's CI is quiet, which is exactly when the fleet sweeps re-poll them; 24h TTL backstop.
- `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` — the token-mint cache, registered OUTSIDE requireAuth (an App JWT cannot resolve `GET /user`): the handler verifies the bearer itself via `ghclient.VerifyAppIdentity` and keys by the app principal. Key: (app id, installation id, SHA-256 of the **canonicalized** request body). Only a 201 whose `expires_at` parses is stored, served until `expires_at - 10min`; rebuild is exactly `{token, expires_at, permissions?, repository_selection?}`. Invalidated on `installation`/`installation_repositories` events. An unverifiable bearer forwards unchanged, uncached. NOT global truth — a minted token is per-credential.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` — the open-PR list (behind reveal), absorbed into (and rebuilt from) the SAME global `pull_requests`/`pr_labels` tables the webhooks maintain — no separate state table. Serving a LIST from rows needs a completeness proof, so a per-repo GLOBAL **"open-PR list complete" marker** (`pulls_list_cache`) gates it: set when an *unfiltered page-1* response absorbs with fewer items than `per_page` (which also reconciles cached open rows the response no longer contains, guarded by the fetch-start grace so a webhook racing the fetch wins); **cleared by `repository` events**; **never touched by `pull_request` events** — those maintain the rows, which is the point (a 24h TTL backstop bounds missed deliveries). A GraphQL sync can add rows that LACK the REST-only columns; the rebuild-time `allRestComplete` gate turns that into a miss rather than serving a hole, so the marker needs no clearing there. Query-shape guard: only `state=open`, `per_page` (1..100), `page=1`, `head=owner:branch`, and `base=<branch>` are modeled — anything else passes through. `head` and `base` are pure FILTERS over the open set the marker already vouches for (given the whole open set, selecting by head or base is exactly what GitHub does), so they are answered from state and, like any filtered response, never SET the marker; the base branch always lives in this repo, so its bare name is the whole filter, unlike `head`, which can name a fork. Pagination guard: a rebuilt list as long as the request's `per_page` is never served from state. Rebuilt item shape (trimmed, exactly a superset of what pr-minder + the pr-minder-reconcile hook read): `{node_id, number, state, title, user{login,type}, body, labels[{name,color}], created_at, updated_at, merge_commit_sha, draft, auto_merge (null | {merge_method}), head{ref,sha,repo:{full_name}|null}, base{ref,sha}}`.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}` — the single-PR read (behind reveal), served from a `pull_requests` row ONLY when the row is **rest-complete** (`ghdata.PRRestComplete`: node_id + base sha present — GraphQL-sourced rows never are), **recently touched** (`ghdata.PRRowFresh`, the 24h staleness backstop for a missed `closed` delivery — `touched_at` is bumped by every webhook/absorb), its **`mergeable` is KNOWN** (MERGEABLE/CONFLICTING), AND its **diff stats are known** (`diffStatsKnown`: additions + deletions both non-NULL). `mergeable` is computed lazily by GitHub and pr-minder polls it to resolution; the known-mergeable gate is what makes caching safe — a null/unknown mergeable ALWAYS misses (fetch + absorb GitHub's computed answer, where a fetched null OVERWRITES via `SetPRMergeable` rather than COALESCE, so the poll keeps reaching GitHub until it resolves). A **branch push un-resolves** `mergeable` on affected open PRs (`NullPRMergeableByBranch`). A fetched CLOSED answer still DELETES any cached open row — the open-only invariant of `pull_requests` is untouched — but is now ABSORBED as a rendered whole-doc snapshot in `closed_pull_cache` and served from it thereafter (every pr-minder drain re-reads settled PRs; each such read used to be a fresh passthrough). The closed doc is the open rebuild's exact shape plus GitHub's real `merged` and its `mergeable` (key always present; typically null), `state` exactly `"closed"` — consumers short-circuit on `pr.state !== 'open'` and read nothing else from a closed PR. It is flushed per PR by EVERY `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` event (a reopen must not serve the stale doc; the REST open absorb also drops it), repo-wide by `repository`, bounded by a 24h TTL — and deliberately NOT flushed by `push` (a push cannot mutate a closed PR). A missed `reopened` delivery can therefore serve the stale closed doc for ≤24h — the same accepted staleness class as `PRRowFresh`, in the opposite direction. Any query string and non-numeric `{number}` segments pass through, as does any non-default `Accept` EXCEPT the diff read (next paragraph). Open rebuild = the list item shape + `{merged: false, mergeable: bool|null, additions: int|null, deletions: int|null}`. **`additions`/`deletions` ride the SINGLE rebuild only** — GitHub's list omits them, so emitting them on a rebuilt list item would invent numbers no upstream answer supplied; the columns have always been absorbed (COALESCEd, so a later list/webhook write cannot blank them) and were simply never served, which is why repo-nightmare read them as `undefined` off the mirror. Nullable-but-always-keyed like `mergeable` (a fabricated `0` reads as "empty PR"), and the `diffStatsKnown` hit gate is what keeps that null off the wire in steady state: a row absorbed from the LIST has no stats while a webhook can resolve its `mergeable` independently, so without the gate such a row would hit and serve `"additions": null` forever with nothing short of a push to heal it. One miss re-absorbs the stats; every later read hits.

  **Merge-field invalidation semantics** (mergeable + merge_commit_sha): a push to a PR's **base or head ⇒ both fields are stale** — GitHub recomputes lazily and never webhooks the result, so `NullPRMergeableByBranch` nulls them AND **remembers the nulled test-merge sha** (`merge_stale_sha`/`merge_stale_at`). A tip change ALWAYS changes the sha of a SUCCESSFUL test merge — a conflicted PR retains its last-good sha and re-offers it with `mergeable:false` — so **an absorb re-offering the remembered sha with mergeable true/unknown is presumed pre-push and can never re-resolve the row**: it stores (and the route serves) unresolved, the row keeps missing — each miss re-triggering GitHub's recompute — until a NEW sha arrives, which resolves and clears the marker (the guard lives in `UpsertPullRequest`'s SQL + `AbsorbSinglePull`, covering the single/list/webhook/sync writers uniformly; the marker rejects only within `ghdata.MergeStaleTTL` ≈ 1h == the strftime `'-1 hour'` cutoffs in the SQL, so a sha wrongly marked stale — absorbed post-recompute before a late push delivery — can't wedge the row into missing forever, and the 24h row TTL stays the outer backstop). The marker also records the **push-tip proof** (`merge_stale_ref`/`merge_stale_after` — the pushed branch and its `after` tip, overwritten by every marking push; NULL when the payload had no usable after): an absorb whose reported tip for that branch equals the push's after sha provably post-dates the push and is **accepted even when it re-offers the remembered sha**, so a WRONG mark — the fresh post-push answer absorbed before the late push delivery landed, then stamped stale by it — heals on the very next poll. A CONFLICTING same-sha answer is instead accepted once the marker outlives `ghdata.MergeStaleConflictingWindow` (30s, the SQL `'-30 seconds'` cutoffs — the dirty-retained pattern: the conflicted PR's frozen base.sha means the tip proof can never fire, and past replica lag the retained sha is the only explanation), so conflicted PRs don't wedge to null after every base push; the `MergeStaleTTL` window is only the backstop for answers that never demonstrate either. Three closed holes (the webhooks#66 frozen-sha incident — a hit never reaches GitHub, so nothing triggered the recompute): the push handler once ran `SetRepoPushedAt` FIRST and returned on its error, skipping the invalidation (it now runs first, each step logs-and-continues); an unparseable push payload skipped it entirely (now: repo-wide `NullPRMergeableByRepo`, deliberately marker-less — the moved branch is unknown and an unmoved PR's re-offered sha is valid); and a recompute-lag refetch could re-resolve the just-invalidated sha permanently — while the sha-less GraphQL owner sync could re-arm `mergeable` via COALESCE on a null/stale-sha REST row (now gated; pure GraphQL rows keep sync-fed mergeable for the /graphql tier).

  The **diff read's 406 verdicts** (`respcache_pulldiff.go`): an Accept that is EXACTLY one media range naming the unified diff (`application/vnd.github.diff` or `.v3.diff`; multi-range Accepts keep the plain passthrough) gets its own flow — pr-minder's `getPullDiff` sends exactly that and branches ONLY on ok/406 (406 = "diff too large" → the files-API fallback; survey 2026-07-11), re-earning the same 406 on every describe hand-off for an oversized PR. The 406 VERDICT is cached per PR (`pull_diff406_cache`, doc `{"message": ...}`, served status 406) behind the SAME `pull` deny kind + resource key as the JSON read (same underlying resource, same authorization). A **200 diff BODY is deliberately never stored** — that would be verbatim byte caching, which the doctrine rejects (an opaque diff has no state to absorb) — so 200s and every other status relay unstored, every time. Flushed per PR by `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` (a head push can shrink the diff back under the boundary), repo-wide by `push`/`repository` (a BASE push can move any PR's three-dot diff across the boundary, with no per-PR signal), + 24h TTL.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation` — the App-level repo-installation lookup (pr-minder's `repoInstallationId`), registered OUTSIDE requireAuth exactly like the mint (App-JWT bearer, self-verified, app principal; `repo_installation_cache` table). Rebuild: `{id, account{login,type}, repository_selection, app_id, app_slug, target_type}`. Invalidated on `installation`/`installation_repositories` events by the stored installation id, plus a 24h TTL. 404 ("not installed") is never stored.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/files` — the PR files listing (behind reveal; pr-minder's `assembleDiffFromFiles` pages it whenever GitHub 406s a too-large unified diff around a describe hand-off — the single largest passthrough slice, ~34%, before this route). Whole-doc per-page snapshots in `pull_files_cache`, keyed `(owner, repo, number, per_page, page)`; trimmed per-file item `{filename, status, additions, deletions, changes, previous_filename?, patch?}` with the PRESENCE of `previous_filename` and `patch` preserved exactly (consumers test `typeof f.patch === 'string'`; GitHub legitimately omits `patch` on binary/oversized files) and the per-file blob `sha` + every URL field dropped. `patch` is unbounded, so a rendered document larger than **1 MiB passes through unstored** (the contents route's cap rule; the 8 MiB fetch cap still bounds the raw body). Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100, default 30) and `page` (1..**40**, default 1 — GitHub's files API stops at 3000 files = 30 pages at the consumers' `per_page=100`, plus margin for the trailing empty page and smaller per_page shapes; raised from 10 in round 2, deeper pages still pass through) only; unknown/repeated params, a non-numeric `{number}` (`/pulls/comments/...`), or a non-default Accept pass through. Only a 200 absorbs, all-or-nothing; an empty array (a page past the end) is a valid cacheable answer. Flushed per PR by EVERY `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` event (head pushes — including fork heads whose push events never arrive — base retargets, reopens), repo-wide by `push`/`repository` (the belt for missed PR deliveries), + 24h TTL.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches` — the branches listing (behind reveal; pr-minder's `listBranchHeads` feeds auto_open_pr fork-point detection, repeated fleet-wide by the reconcile hook — ~18% of passthroughs before this route). Whole-doc per-page snapshots in `branches_list_cache`, keyed `(owner, repo, per_page, page)`; trimmed item `{name, commit:{sha}, protected}` (consumers read `name` + `commit.sha`; `protected` rides along as an always-present bool) with `commit.url`, the protection object, and `protection_url` dropped. Same shape guard as the files route (`per_page`/`page` only); the single-branch `/branches/{branch}` read is a different shape and stays passthrough. Only a 200 absorbs; empty array cacheable. Branch create, delete, and tip-move all arrive as push events, so `push`/`repository` flush repo-wide, + 24h TTL.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>` (`respcache_actionsruns.go`) — the per-sha workflow-runs listing (behind reveal; survey 2026-07-11: pr-minder's `hasWorkflowRuns` sends `?head_sha=<hex>&per_page=1` and reads ONLY `total_count` — the zombie probe, repeated fleet-wide — and required-builds' `listWorkflowRuns` pages `?head_sha=<hex>&per_page=100&page=N` reading name/status/conclusion/html_url). Whole-doc snapshots in `workflow_runs_cache`, keyed `(owner, repo, head_sha, per_page, page)`. **`head_sha` is REQUIRED for a cacheable shape** — non-empty, full hex, lowercase-normalized into the key; the UNFILTERED listing churns with every run anywhere in the repo and is deliberately unmodeled (passthrough), as is every other filter param (`branch`/`event`/`status`/`actor`/`created`/...); deeper `/actions/runs/{id}/...` paths never reach the exact-literal registration and keep falling to the NotFound proxy. Rebuild: `{total_count, workflow_runs:[{id, name, head_sha, status, conclusion, html_url, created_at, updated_at, run_started_at}]}` — **`total_count` is copied VERBATIM from upstream** (GitHub's TOTAL matching-run count, NOT the page length — exactly what the `per_page=1` probe reads); name/conclusion/run_started_at nullable with keys always emitted; `html_url` a pinned consumer-read allowlist exception (required-builds links the run). Absorb gate: 200 + object + `total_count` and `workflow_runs` both PRESENT; per run id > 0, non-empty status, full-hex head_sha; the zero-runs answer (`total_count: 0`, empty array) is cacheable — it IS the zombie probe's verdict. Staleness: run creation/state changes fire `check_suite`/`check_run`/`workflow_job` events within seconds and the dispatcher flushes the sha's pages on all of them (queued/waiting `workflow_job` deliveries included — invalidation precedes the disposition logic), and a `workflow_run` delivery flushes them too — the only signal for a `startup_failure` run, which creates no jobs, check runs, or statuses (needs the App subscribed to `workflow_run`; until then that window is bounded by the TTL); run DELETION emits no webhook at all → bounded by the 24h TTL, acceptable because both consumers fail safe on a stale answer (pr-minder's revive is additionally guarded by its commit-age deferral); `repository` flushes repo-wide.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` — the bare repository read (behind reveal; the reconcile hook's `getDefaultBranch`, plus status-only access checks in the buildhost `canAccessRepo` style, where the 200-vs-404 IS the answer). UNLIKE every other cached route there is NO snapshot table and NO per-row TTL: the rebuild comes straight from the `repos` TRUTH row — the same webhook-maintained, fleet-synced, consistency-checked state tier 1 serves — so truth freshness IS the freshness model (mirroring how `/graphql` serves truth; `repository` events correct rename/delete/visibility, and a reveal probe re-absorbs the row per principal within the ≤24h grant TTL, which bounds how stale a private repo's row can sit for a probing caller). Served only when the row can answer COMPLETELY: known visibility (unknown `''` fails CLOSED — e.g. a row seeded only by the identity-locked GraphQL fetch, which carries no visibility), a known `default_branch`, and a canonical full name; anything else fetches with the caller's token and the absorbed 200 heals the row. Trimmed rebuild: `{name, full_name, owner:{login}, private, visibility, default_branch, archived, disabled}` — `private` derived (visibility != public, so `internal` folds to private=true); `pushed_at` deliberately NOT emitted (truth `''` cannot distinguish never-pushed from not-yet-synced, and no consumer reads it); `fork`/`id` not stored, so not emitted. Query params, non-default Accepts, and HEAD requests (MethodNotAllowed → the proxy) pass through; a non-200 fetch relays unstored.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/{ref...}` (`respcache_gitrefs.go`) — the ref-to-tip lookup ("where does this branch point right now"), the largest UNROUTED slice of the request log before it existed: fleet reconcile passes ask it per branch, forever. The wildcard is greedy (a ref path is at least `heads/<name>` and branch names carry slashes) and the ref is stored **VERBATIM, never resolved** — `heads/main` and `refs/heads/main` are distinct requests, so each is its own row and the push flush covers every spelling (`refSpellings`). Rebuild: `{ref, node_id, object:{sha, type}}` — the canonical ref name GitHub reported, a stable identifier, and the object trimmed to sha + type; `url` and `object.url` dropped. Shape guard: no query parameter changes this answer so any is unmodeled, and the ref must be a fully-qualified two-part ref (`heads/<name>`, `tags/<name>`, with or without the `refs/` prefix) — GitHub answers a PARTIAL ref (`heads`) with an ARRAY, a different shape this route does not hold. The **404 is absorbed as a VERDICT** on the compare route's precedent (sweeps re-poll deleted heads — a merged PR's head — forever), and it cannot outlive the ref: ref creation arrives as a push for that exact ref, which drops the row. Invalidation: per-ref (every spelling) by `push`, repo-wide by `repository` and by a push whose payload names no usable ref, + 24h TTL.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` + `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}` (`respcache_workflowjobs.go`, one `workflow_jobs_cache` row space, kinds `run_jobs`/`job`) — **only TERMINAL answers are stored**: a jobs page whose every job has `completed`, or a single completed job. A queued/in_progress job is a LIVE value the GHA runner coordinator provisions against — serving one even seconds stale could over- or under-provision runners — and no TTL short enough to be safe there would be long enough to be worth having, so those always reach GitHub (recorded `unmodeled-response`). One in-flight job makes the WHOLE page live: the page is the answer. What this kills is the fleet re-reading SETTLED runs forever — the closed-PR cache's stance applied to Actions. A finished run can still change, because a **RE-RUN replaces its jobs under the same run id**, so both kinds carry the owning `run_id` and `workflow_job`/`workflow_run` deliveries flush every row under that run (repo-wide when the payload names none); `repository` flushes repo-wide; 24h TTL. Rebuild: `{total_count, jobs:[…]}` / one job of `{id, run_id, run_attempt, workflow_name, head_branch, head_sha, name, status, conclusion, created_at, started_at, completed_at, labels, runner_name, steps:[{name,status,conclusion,number,started_at,completed_at}]}` — nullables always keyed, every URL field dropped (no consumer survey has pinned one here). Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100) and `page` (1..10) only — `filter=latest|all` selects a DIFFERENT job set for a re-run and stays unmodeled.
- `GET /orgs/{org}/installation` + `GET /users/{username}/installation` (`respcache_installation.go`) — the OWNER-level installation lookups answer the same object as the repo-level one for an account rather than a repository, on the same App-JWT terms (registered OUTSIDE `requireAuth`, bearer self-verified, keyed by the verified app id). They reuse that route's absorb, rebuild, row space, and invalidation: a row is keyed (app actor, owner, repo), so an owner-level answer is stored under a **sentinel repo value** no real repository can collide with (`*org` / `*user` — `*` is illegal in a GitHub repo name). Two sentinels because they are two questions: an account can answer one and 404 the other. 404 ("not installed") is never stored — an app can be installed a moment later. Invalidated by `installation`/`installation_repositories` on the stored installation id, + 24h TTL.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/commits` (`respcache_pullcommits.go`) — GitHub answers it with the SAME item shape as the repository commits list, so this route **reuses that storage whole**: the listed commits are upserted into the one global `git_commits_cache`, and the page's ordered shas become a `commits_list_cache` snapshot under the synthetic ref key `pull/<number>/commits`. That is the resource those rows already model (an ordered list of commits under a key), and it inherits the immutable-commit synergy, the hit gate (every listed sha must still resolve), the pruning, and the rebuild unchanged; a caller cannot collide with the key, which would require `?sha=pull/<n>/commits` on the repo commits list — a ref that resolves to nothing and is never stored. Reveal uses the single-PR route's deny kind and resource key (same resource, same authorization question). Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100) and `page` (1..10) only. Invalidation follows the PR-files route, which has the identical fork-head problem: every `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` delivery flushes that ONE PR, a `push` flushes the repo's PR-commit snapshots as the belt for a missed delivery, `repository` repo-wide, + the shared 24h TTL. The dispatcher restates the key literal (a sync -> api import would be a cycle); both sides pin it and an end-to-end flush test proves they meet.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-quality/setup` (`respcache_codequality.go`) — GitHub Code Quality's per-repo enablement configuration, a large uncached slice of the request log (a fleet sweep asking "is this repo enrolled", per repo). Modeled from GitHub's OpenAPI description (schema `code-quality-setup`, public preview — [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-quality/code-quality#get-a-code-quality-setup-configuration)) rather than from a captured sample. The endpoint takes no query parameters, so the repo is the whole key; the rebuild is the whole documented record — `{state, languages, runner_type, runner_label, updated_at, schedule, ai_findings_option}` — because the schema carries no URL field to drop, with every nullable keyed and `languages` always an array. `state: not-configured` is a real cacheable verdict (it IS what the sweep asks). Non-200s (403 "not available here", 404, 503) relay unstored and are deliberately NOT cached as verdicts: unlike a missing git ref, nothing observable says when the feature becomes available.

  **Staleness, stated plainly:** this is CONFIG and GitHub emits no webhook when it changes. The mirror sees exactly one change signal — a `PATCH` to the same path that it proxies, which is why the PATCH is registered at all: the handler flushes the row and then forwards, so a caller cannot read its own stale config. (The flush runs BEFORE forwarding on purpose: a failed PATCH that dropped the row costs one miss, while a successful PATCH whose flush was skipped serves a wrong answer for the whole TTL.) `repository` events flush repo-wide. A change made in the UI, or by a client that does not go through the mirror, is invisible until the TTL — which is therefore **1 hour**, not the usual 24.

## Deliberately NOT cached

Recording the verdict is part of the job: a route left uncached for a reason
should not be rediscovered as a "gap" every time someone reads the Requests
tab. These describe sets that change continuously with no webhook naming the
change, so any TTL long enough to help would serve wrong answers.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` WITHOUT `head_sha` — the GHA runner
  coordinator's queued-backlog poll (`?status=queued&per_page=…`), the single
  largest passthrough slice in the log. It is a real-time work queue: the
  coordinator provisions runners against it, and the unfiltered listing also
  churns with every run anywhere in the repo. The `head_sha`-filtered shape IS
  cached (above).
- `GET /orgs/{org}/actions/runners` — a live runner roster, same reasoning.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and
  `/actions/jobs/{id}` while any job is queued or in progress — the routes
  exist but store only terminal answers, for the same reason.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks`, `GET /orgs/{org}/hooks` — webhook
  configuration lists. Hook create/edit has no reliable delivery to us, and a
  consumer reconciling hooks off a stale listing would create duplicates.
  Cacheable in principle; needs a consumer survey first.

Two more are simply unmodeled for want of evidence rather than by verdict, and
`GET /api/brief` is how to get it: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-quality/setup`
(a large slice whose response shape nothing here has yet observed) and
`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels/{name}` (a small one, with a clean `label`
webhook signal available).
